title: Kyoto at Lincoln Center #kyotoplay #lincolncentertheater #kyotoclimat...
transcript: Kyoto is a new play about the Kyoto climate conference in 1997 and the years of negotiations leading up to it. Written by Joe Murphy and Joe Robertson, the duo behind The Jungle, this play is similarly complex and sprawling, but I found this one harder to emotionally invest in. I might just be burnt out by our dysfunctional political landscape, but this piece was really close for comfort. Watching these diplomats debate and quarrel about evidence-based climate science is kind of painful when you know that years later, even stronger evidence will still be debated. But I would say this is a good play in that it got me to think. It illuminates the massive complexity of the problem and a myriad of human reactions to it. While there are definitely some hopeful takeaways, I found it hard to ignore the overwhelming propensity toward greed and short-term gains over long-term progress that so many nations exemplified during the events portrayed in this play. But I think that's very intentional, and we're meant to acknowledge our own complicity too, as reflected by the fact that the central character of the play is definitely not the good guy. If political dramas are your thing, or if you want to see a piece about a subject that can always use more public consciousness, Kyoto is running at Lincoln Centre through November 30th. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer found it hard to emotionally invest and close-to-home painful, but calls it a good play that provokes thought and recommends it for fans of political drama.
